title: Jacky Chou on SEO after a $500K/month wipeout: link tactics, AI citations, CRO and launching fast
summary: Jacky Chou explains how he rebuilt after Google wiped out his 15-site partnership business (about $500K/month). He covers white/gray/black hat link building, CTR signals, getting cited by AI, and how he launches and bundles software. He also gives CRO rules for paid landing pages.

principles.text: Never trust a guru's tactic until you've tested it on multiple sites; anyone whose claims fail repeatedly is written off.
principles.quote: you have to always validate it. You can't just like assume that people what people are telling you is the truth.

principles.text: Launch fast, check for product-market fit with your audience, then go all in; otherwise kill the product or leave it on autopilot.
principles.quote: I validate it, make sure there's a product market fit within my audience. If there's a fit, then I go all in on it.

principles.text: Compete in mature software markets by bundling many features under one subscription rather than being best at any one.
principles.quote: It's like the Adobe approach. We just give everything under one subscription.

principles.text: Keep the core money site clean of mass AI content, because blasting thousands of articles exposes you to a destroyed business.
principles.quote: a huge fan of uh spamming hundreds of blog posts on a money site where I need that to like last forever

principles.text: Paid traffic needs a dedicated, stripped-down landing page with no nav, so the only actions are convert or leave.
principles.quote: if you're running paid ads, you need a dedicated landing page. Do not send it to your home page.

principles.text: Consistency beats talent: sticking with one thing daily for 90 days will get most people to $10K/month.
principles.quote: if they stick to anything for 90 days, they're 100% make 10k per month.
